newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper urges interbank forex lending market.
newsitem.headline: China paper urges interbank forex lending market.

text.p: An official newspaper on Wednesday urged Beijing to quickly set up a national market for banks to lend and borrow short-term foreign exchange funds among themselves and proposed Shanghai as the venue.
The Shanghai-based Business News said China's foreign exchange market was imperfect without such an interbank foreign exchange lending market.

Chinese banks cannot make good use of their surplus foreign exchange at present and cannot cover short-term shortages because foreign currencies are allowed to flow only within a bank and not among different banks, it said.

China has an interbank foreign exchange trading market based in Shanghai to trade U.S. and Hong Kong dollars and yen against the yuan. It also has a national yuan interbank lending market launched early this year.

"Foreign exchange lending business is an important part of a foreign exchange market," the paper said. "To set up an interbank foreign exchange lending market would be an important step for China's financial reforms."

The paper said Beijing had allowed branches of overseas banks to settle foreign exchange accounts for foreign-invested firms in China since July 1, making the set-up of such a foreign exchange market even more urgent.
It said the proposed market could be open to designated banks and financial departments of major companies in its initial stages before being open to all major financial institutions.

The paper mentioned Shanghai's financial background and that Beijing aimed to build the city into an international financial centre. The city would be a good place to host the interbank foreign exchange lending market, it added.
